Plan: Verbose console logging and a timestamped log file¶

Issue: #14 — Usability: add verbose console logging with an output timestamped logfile Branch: 14-verbose-logging (from main at 5688d28) Status: steps 1–4 committed. Step 5 (README) skipped at the user’s request (2026-10-18). Step 6 (GUI testing) remains. The open questions are decided (section 7, 2026-10-18).

1. Goal¶

From the issue:

  • A runtime flag -v / --verbose prints log messages about application actions to the console.

  • The flag takes an optional level (DEBUG, INFO, WARNING, ERROR) that sets the minimum level printed.

  • Every run always writes a log file, wvt_log_<date>_<time>.log, whether or not -v is given. The issue names /tmp; the file goes to $TMPDIR (fallback /tmp) so that it works the same on macOS and Linux (section 7).

Checklist from the issue, mapped to sections below:

Issue item

Section

Add log statements to actions, with levels

5

Print logs to console

3, 4

Save logs to file

3, 4

Out of scope: an in-GUI log viewer window, log rotation / cleanup of old files (the OS clears the temp folder), syslog / journald, and a TRACE level for per-block signal-processing output.

2. Starting point¶

Area

What exists

Gap

Console output

~95 fprintf(stderr, "wvt: ...") calls, all in src/app/main.cpp (arg errors, headless record / audio / siggen progress, device errors)

No levels, nothing goes to a file

Library code

engine, live, recorder, sdr_*, siggen_out, audio_* print nothing; they return errors via std::string& err or stats().error / status() fields that the GUI shows

Actions (device start, tune, record start/stop, gaps, TX, audio start) leave no trace

Threads

live, recorder, sdr_rtlsdr, sdr_uhd, sdr_sim, siggen_out, audio_engine, dsp all run worker threads

Logger must be thread-safe

Real-time path

miniaudio callback in audio_out.cpp, SDR RX callbacks

Must not block on a mutex or do file I/O there

Timestamps

recorder.cpp / wav_writer.cpp use strftime("%Y%m%d_%H%M%S") on gmtime_r

Reuse the same stamp format for the log name

CLI

Hand-rolled loop in main() with a next() lambda; -v is unused

Need an optional value, which the loop does not support yet

3. Design decisions¶

Topic

Decision

Reason

Library

Small in-house src/common/log.h / src/common/log.cpp (~150 lines), no new dependency

Matches the vendored, no-network build; spdlog would be overkill

Levels

DEBUG < INFO < WARN < ERROR (accept WARNING as an alias, case-insensitive)

The “standard message types” in the issue

Console default

Without -v: WARN and ERROR still print (keeps today’s error messages). -v alone = INFO. -v LEVEL = that level

No change in behavior for users who don’t pass -v (decided, section 7)

File level

The file always gets DEBUG and up, independent of -v

Issue: “always generate a log file of those verbose actions”. The file is for after-the-fact debugging

Optional value parsing

--verbose=LEVEL, -v LEVEL, -vLEVEL. With a space, the next token is taken as the level only if it is a known level name; otherwise it is left for the file / next option

wvt -v rec.sigmf-meta must still open the file

File location

First match of: --log-dir DIR, $WVT_LOG_DIR, $TMPDIR, /tmp. --no-log-file turns it off

$TMPDIR is the per-user temp folder on macOS (/var/folders/...) and is usually unset on Linux, so the fallback gives /tmp there. The overrides help read-only or shared machines (decided, section 7)

File name

wvt_log_<YYYYMMDD>_<HHMMSS>.log, local time. If the name exists (two runs in one second) append _<pid>

Local time matches what the user sees on the clock; strftime format matches the recorder

Line format

File: 2026-10-18 14:08:37.123 [INFO ] [live] streaming from rtlsdr:0, 2.4 MS/s at 915 MHz. Console with -v: same without the date. Console without -v: today’s wvt: <msg> (WARN: wvt: warning: <msg>)

Sortable, greppable; the [component] tag shows where it came from. The plain console format keeps the output of users who don’t pass -v unchanged

Thread safety

One mutex around the write of each formatted line; format outside the lock

Simple. Log volume is low (actions, not per-sample)

Who logs an error

An error that returns through err or a status field is logged at ERROR once, by the code that shows it to the user (main.cpp, app*.cpp). Library code logs the same failure at DEBUG for context. Library WARN only for problems nothing else reports (dropped samples, clamped gain, metadata rewrite failures, TX notes)

Without this rule one failure printed two or three times on the default console

Real-time paths

No logging inside the audio callback or SDR sample callbacks. Count events there (underruns, gaps) with atomics and log a summary from the worker / UI thread

Keeps the audio and RX paths lock-free

Header line

First lines of the file: wvt version / git hash, build options (RTL-SDR / UHD / audio on or off), full command line, OS

Makes a log file useful on its own in a bug report

Failure to open the file

Print one WARN to stderr and continue with console only

Logging must never stop the app

Flush

Flush after WARN/ERROR lines and at exit; also flush on SIGINT/SIGTERM in headless mode

Lines are not lost on Ctrl+C or a crash after an error

API shape

Free functions logInit(cfg), logWrite(LogLevel, "component", fmt, ...) printf-style, logParseArgs(), plus macros LOG_DEBUG("live", ...) etc. that skip formatting when no sink takes the level

The code base uses no namespaces (fmtSI, parseSI), and a log namespace clashes with ::log from <cmath>. printf style matches the existing fprintf code; the macro check keeps DEBUG cheap

4. Implementation steps¶

  1. Logger core — done. src/common/log.h, src/common/log.cpp; add to wvt, siggen_check and audio_check in CMakeLists.txt (the tools link library sources that will now call the logger; the tools do not call init, so they get console WARN+ and no file).

  2. CLI in src/app/main.cpp — done (logParseArgs() strips the log options from argv; the git revision for the header comes from git describe at configure time):

    • Parse -v / --verbose[=LEVEL], --log-dir, --no-log-file as the first pass over argv, then call log::init() before the main parse loop, so arg errors are logged too.

    • Add the options to usage() and print the log file path at INFO on start.

  3. Convert main.cpp output — done. Replace fprintf(stderr, "wvt: ...") error / status calls with LOG_ERROR / LOG_WARN / LOG_INFO. Keep as plain printf/fprintf: usage(), --list-devices, --list-audio-devices, and the \r progress line of headless recording (it is a live display, not a log). Log a progress summary to the file at DEBUG instead, once every few seconds.

    • As built: messages that printed without -v before (“streaming from”, “recording to”, “wrote”, “metadata”, “TRANSMITTING”, “screenshot written”) use logStatus(): always on the console, INFO in the file. Default console output is byte-for-byte the same as before.

    • The \r lines use logProgress() / logProgressEnd(): always on the console, DEBUG in the file at most every 10 s. A log line that arrives while a progress line is open starts on a new line, so step 4 logs from worker threads don’t garble it.

    • wvt: note: ... messages became WARN (wvt: warning: ...). Arg errors are ERROR.

    • New INFO lines for the GUI path: window size / renderer, device start, file open, exit.

  4. Add action logs to the library code (section 5) — done.

    • sdr_device.cpp logs every open centrally (requested vs actual rate / fc, notes), so each backend only adds DEBUG detail (uhd: open, tune result, packet size, gain clamp; rtlsdr: USB strings, tuner, gain steps, transfer size).

    • live: start/stop summary, retune, gain, spectrum settings (DEBUG), dropped-sample summary at most every 5 s from the spectrum thread, and the device stopping on its own.

    • recorder: start, end summary (reason, bytes, gaps, lost samples), retune segments and the first 50 gaps (DEBUG), writer lag high-water mark (DEBUG).

    • siggen_out: file generation start/end; TX start, retune, gain, stop summary (underflows, lost packets).

    • audio_engine: start (mode, channel, output), stop summary (underruns, resyncs), WAV start/close, WAV export. Nothing in the miniaudio callback; it only counts underruns.

    • engine: Worker logs jobs that take 250 ms or more (DEBUG). Logging every recompute would add many lines a second while panning (section 7: no DSP detail for now).

    • iq_file: metadata guess result and file open (DEBUG).

    • app*.cpp: ERROR at each place an error reaches the status bar, plus a recording that fails on its own (edge-detected in pollLive()); INFO for opened files.

    • Found while doing this: openDevice() discarded the warning from checkSampleRate() (e.g. UHD above 8 MS/s needs USB 3). It is now in the log at DEBUG; the GUI still doesn’t show it for UHD (RTL-SDR folds it into notes()).

  5. Docs — skipped (2026-10-18). README: a short Logging section (flag, levels, file location, what to attach to a bug report).

  6. Test (section 6).

5. What to log¶

Component

INFO

DEBUG

WARN / ERROR

main / app

start-up, log path, file opened (path, format, rate, fc, size), window size / renderer (GLX or software), exit

parsed CLI overrides, SigMF / filename auto-detection results

bad args, file open failure, GLX fallback

engine / dsp

—

FFT size, decimation, view changes, recompute timings (once per recompute, not per block)

cancelled / failed compute

live + sdr_*

device open (type, serial), stream start/stop, retune, gain / antenna / bandwidth changes

actual vs requested rate & fc, buffer sizes

device errors, overflow / dropped samples (summarised)

recorder

record start (paths, format), stop (duration, bytes, gaps)

ring fill high-water mark

write errors, gaps

siggen / siggen_out

waveform mode + key params, file gen start/finish, loopback start/stop, TX start/stop, tx gain

per-pulse schedule summary

TX errors, underruns

audio_*

mode, channel, output device, start/stop, WAV export path

resampler ratio / PI loop corrections

device open failure, underrun count (summarised)

UI

—

window open/close (siggen, audio), screenshot path

—

Where the code already builds an err string or sets stats().error, log it at the point it is set, so the GUI and the log show the same text.

6. Testing¶

  • Unit-ish (add to tools/, or a small log_check): level parsing incl. WARNING alias and case; filtering per level; file gets DEBUG while console is at WARN; name collision gets _<pid>; concurrent logging from 8 threads gives no interleaved lines.

  • CLI: wvt -v file, wvt -v debug file, wvt --verbose=error file, wvt -vDEBUG, wvt -v with a file literally named debug (documented edge case: use ./debug).

  • Headless: --device sim --record x --no-gui --record-duration 3 → log has start, stop, byte count; Ctrl+C mid-run still leaves a complete file.

  • No regressions: run siggen_check and audio_check; output without -v matches today.

  • Log location: $TMPDIR set (macOS) → file there; $TMPDIR unset (typical Linux) → /tmp; $WVT_LOG_DIR and --log-dir override in that order; directory not writable → one warning, app still runs.

  • Platforms: macOS (XQuartz) and Linux.

7. Decisions (2026-10-18)¶

Question

Decision

Console level without -v

Stay at WARN and up, as today. -v / -v LEVEL only lowers it

Log directory

Use $TMPDIR, fall back to /tmp when it is unset, for cross-platform behavior. --log-dir and $WVT_LOG_DIR still override

Old log files

No cleanup in wvt. The OS clears the temp folder

Signal-processing detail (TRACE)

Left out for now. DSP logs stay at one DEBUG line per recompute; no per-block output
